source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 15: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
\(x^2 - 2x + 2 = (x - 1)^2 + 1\) is irreducible and squared: Case-IV. Degree 2 < degree 4, so proper.
Split into \(\frac{Ax + B}{x^2 - 2x + 2} + \frac{Cx + D}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\), then put \(t = x - 1\) to integrate.
Plan: constants by comparing coefficients; integrate each piece; the squared piece is done with \(t = \tan\theta\) as in Example 43.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x^2 + 1}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\,dx\).
To find: the integral.
Method: partial fractions, Case-IV; discriminant of \(x^2 - 2x + 2\) is \(4 - 8 = -4 < 0\), so it is irreducible.

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{x^2 + 1}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2} = \dfrac{Ax + B}{x^2 - 2x + 2} + \dfrac{Cx + D}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\]
\[x^2 + 1 = (Ax + B)(x^2 - 2x + 2) + Cx + D\]
Why: A linear numerator for each power of the repeated quadratic factor.

Rewrite the integrand
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 2} + \dfrac{2x - 1}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 2} + \dfrac{2x - 2}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2} + \dfrac{1}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\]
Why: \(2x - 2\) is the derivative of \(x^2 - 2x + 2\), so split \(2x - 1 = (2x - 2) + 1\).

First two pieces
\[\int \dfrac{dx}{(x - 1)^2 + 1} = \tan^{-1}(x - 1)\]
\[\int \dfrac{2x - 2}{(x^2 - 2x + 2)^2}\,dx = -\dfrac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 2}\]
Why: Completing the square; and \(\int u^{-2}\,du = -u^{-1}\) with \(u = x^2 - 2x + 2\).

Last piece (put \(t = x - 1 = \tan\theta\))
\[\int \dfrac{dx}{\left((x - 1)^2 + 1\right)^2} = \int \dfrac{dt}{(t^2 + 1)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\tan^{-1} t + \dfrac{t}{t^2 + 1}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(x - 1) + \dfrac{x - 1}{2(x^2 - 2x + 2)}\]
Why: Same as Example 43: \(\int \cos^2\theta\,d\theta = \frac{1}{2}(\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta)\) and \(\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{t}{1 + t^2}\).

Check by differentiating (with \(t = x - 1\), \(q = t^2 + 1\))
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\tan^{-1} t + \dfrac{t - 2}{2q}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2q} + \dfrac{q - 2t(t - 2)}{2q^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3q + q - 2t^2 + 4t}{2q^2} = \dfrac{t^2 + 2t + 2}{q^2}\]
Why: \(t^2 + 2t + 2 = (x - 1)^2 + 2(x - 1) + 2 = x^2 + 1\) and \(q = x^2 - 2x + 2\): the integrand \(\checkmark\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answers at the end of the book (pages 301-302, printed under the heading "Exercise 3.6") stop at item (xiv); no answer is printed for Question 15. The correct answer, checked by differentiation, is \(\frac{3}{2}\tan^{-1}(x - 1) + \frac{x - 3}{2(x^2 - 2x + 2)} + c\).
